data.symptom: Customers' webhook endpoints are paused after repeated failures although their servers were up. Each pause starts at the top of the hour, when the endpoint's OAuth token expires during the hourly burst of events.
impact: Customers' downstream systems missed task events until support replayed them.
One customer's security team blocked our OAuth client as a possible compromise.

evidence.point: Every storm began at a token expiry with 26 to 32 deliveries in flight.
Every delivery in flight asked for its own token and retried at once, so each new token revoked the last.
evidence.quote: 32 threads each request a new token (no shared refresh)

evidence.point: No delivery reached Saffron Foods before the pause; only token requests went out.
19 of 212 burst expiries hit the customer's rate limit, and those are the 19 OAuth pauses; HMAC endpoints sent no token requests.

hypotheses.statement: Each delivery thread refreshes an expired token on its own and retries without backoff, so the customer's identity provider rate-limits our client and the endpoint is paused.
supports: Seen directly in the ep_harbor_main log.
Every storm starts at a token expiry during a burst.
against_or_gaps: The customer's identity provider logs are second-hand.
Only two storms have our full logs.

hypotheses.statement: The customers' identity providers revoke tokens early under load, which makes our retries fail. May coexist with the first.
supports: Some retries got 401 with a fresh token.
Two customers' identity providers rate-limited us.
against_or_gaps: One active token per client explains the 401s.
Quiet expiries refresh with one request.

ruled_out: An outage of the customer's identity provider
open_questions: Should the worker refresh an endpoint's token once, for every thread?
Should a 429 from a token endpoint count toward the pause?
Do other OAuth customers' identity providers keep one active token per client?

data.title: Webhook endpoints paused by a token-refresh storm
data.scope: 7 tickets, 5 accounts, OAuth endpoints only, 21 days.
reproduction: Run the lab's reproduction test with the fix flag off: 32 deliveries meet an expired token on the hour.
It passes by showing the bug: over 100 token requests in a minute, a 429, and the endpoint paused while it is up.
Compare with the ep_harbor_main log: 401s, one token request per thread, retries at once, then the pause.
Ask one affected customer's identity provider admin for their token rate limit and their one-token-per-client setting.
evidence_attached: Lab tests: storm reproduced; regression fails without the fix
ruled_out: An outage of the customer's identity provider
data.workaround_in_place: Support replays paused endpoints with RB-14 after a test delivery and keeps the tickets on the incident; a proposed detector flags new storms within 15 minutes.
data.the_ask: Decide how the webhook worker should refresh an expired token once per endpoint, and how deliveries should wait instead of failing when the customer's identity provider rate-limits token requests.
data.hypothesis_note: The token-refresh storm is reproduced in a lab with a scripted identity provider and endpoint. How each customer's identity provider limits token requests is not confirmed.

applies_when: Endpoint paused at the top of the hour while the customer's server was up.

how_to_confirm: Delivery log: 401 on every delivery in flight right after a token expiry.

Endpoint uses OAuth client credentials, not an HMAC signature.
steps: Confirm the customer's endpoint answers 200 to a test delivery, before RB-14.

Link the ticket to the parent incident and tell the customer the requests were ours.

escalate_if: The endpoint still fails a test delivery.
The endpoint uses an HMAC signature, not OAuth.
A security team reports requests from addresses that are not ours.
